args.author: agent:xenobot
args.body: GBIF holds 16,295 occurrence records for Xenopus laevis (Daudin, 1802), concentrated in BE, ZA, US. In the Western Cape, South Africa GBIF holds 20,688 records; the 8 most-recorded non-Aves species are listed. None of the 35 taxa GloBI records as eating Xenopus laevis (Daudin, 1802) appear in this box's top 8 by record count. Read that as a gap in two databases before reading it as an empty niche: the box list is truncated, record-ranked and missing every Aves species. No population parameters were declared, so whether this design could establish against what is there has NOT been evaluated. That question needs numbers no occurrence database contains. Every number here is about Xenopus laevis. A xenobot is 0.5 mm of ciliated donor tissue with no mouth, no gut, no gonads and a working life of days; it shares the genome and nothing else that an ecologist would use. Transferring this community, these predators or this range to the construct would be the error this whole run is about, so the run states the records and does not transfer them.

detail.recorded_range: GBIF holds 16,295 occurrence records for Xenopus laevis (Daudin, 1802), concentrated in BE, ZA, US.
cannot_say: whether the design would be outcompeted: that needs growth rates, carrying capacities and competition coefficients, and none of them is in an occurrence record or an interaction record
how abundant anything is: occurrence counts are records, which is sampling effort as much as biology
whether the design could eat what is there, or be eaten by what is there: the interaction records are for its CLADE, and a design is by construction not its clade
anything about the places nobody has surveyed, which is most places
anything about Aves, which is filtered out of every result here by design and is a central part of most terrestrial communities

result.scope: A co-design log. Agents post proposals; a human role approves or rejects them (session_decide); only human roles edit directly. Applied edits record the Lean verdicts at the time (floating point, not a kernel check) and the lawset version used. Authors are role labels, not people.
